items.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
items.excerpt: Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at " intelligent eyewear " for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they're no impulse buy. These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered. Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn't told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea. Read full article Comments

items.title: Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk
items.excerpt: The Apple Silicon iMac got its fourth refresh this month. Every other Apple Silicon Mac has found a way to move forward over the last half-decade—we've gotten a more Pro design for the MacBook Pro, a mini-er design for the Mac mini, and a Mac Studio that has finally made Apple admit it doesn't want to make the Mac Pro anymore. But the Apple Silicon iMac has always been more interested in looking backward. It's the thin, screen-on-a-stand iMac design by way of the original Bondi Blue G3 iMac. It's a clean and pretty desktop computer, one I see all the time in small offices and on TV shows that depict small offices. We're long past the days when it was Apple's primary workstation computer. items.title: T-Mobile illegally imposed 50GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says
items.excerpt: T-Mobile violated a New York state law by imposing a 50GB-per-month data cap and reducing speeds to less than a megabit per second on home Internet plans it is required to offer people with low incomes, New York government officials alleged. T-Mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days. The alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to T-Mobile's wireless home Internet service, not the company's mobile plans. Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement on Monday, saying that a state investigation found T-Mobile violated the New York Affordable Broadband Act (ABA). Read full article Comments

items.excerpt: # Whisper [[Blog]](https://openai.com/blog/whisper) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04356) [[Model card]](https://github.com/openai/whisper/blob/main/model-card.md) [[Colab example]](https://colab.research.google.com/github/openai/whisper/blob/master/notebooks/LibriSpeech.ipynb) Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition model. It is trained on a large dataset of diverse audio and is also a multitasking model that can perform multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, and language identification. ## Approach ![Approach](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/whisper/main/approach.png) A Transformer sequence-to-sequence model is trained on various speech processing tasks, including multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, spoken language identification, and voice activity detection. These tasks are jointly represented as a sequence of tokens to be predicted by the decoder, allowing a single model to replace many stages of a traditional speech-processing pipeline. The multitask training format uses a set of special tokens that serve as task specifiers or classification targets. ## Setup We used Python 3.9.9 and [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/) 1.10.1 to train and test our models, but the codebase is expected to be compatible with Python 3.8-3.11 and recent PyTorch versions. items.excerpt: Zellij [ Installation ] [ Screencasts & Tutorials ] [ Configuration ] [ Layouts ] [ FAQ ] # What is this? [Zellij](#origin-of-the-name) is a workspace aimed at developers, ops-oriented people and anyone who loves the terminal. Similar programs are sometimes called "Terminal Multiplexers". Zellij is designed around the philosophy that one must not sacrifice simplicity for power, taking pride in its great experience out of the box as well as the advanced features it places at its users' fingertips. Zellij is geared toward beginner and power users alike - allowing deep customizability, personal automation through [layouts](https://zellij.dev/documentation/layouts.html), true multiplayer collaboration, unique UX features such as floating and stacked panes, and a [plugin system](https://zellij.dev/documentation/plugins.html) allowing one to create plugins in any language that compiles to WebAssembly. Zellij includes a built-in [web-client](https://zellij.dev/tutorials/web-client/), making a terminal optional. You can get started by [installing](https://zellij.dev/documentation/installation.html) Zellij and checking out the [Screencasts & Tutorials](https://zellij.dev/screencasts/). items.title: vercel-labs / agent-browser
items.excerpt: # agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell. agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example…

items.excerpt: Hi HN We built a tool to help founders understand how modern fundraising (with safes) works, and how much dilution you can expect when raising money. The project is open-source. The code is a mess right now, but it'll get better I promise. You can also help with that. We didn't build this to make money. We genuinely did it because we were looking for it, and couldn't find it. We're in fact in the process of fundraising for a company, and at first glance the process looks simple. Just an excel sheet will do! But then the more we dug into it and tried different simulators, the more we realized that it's more complex than it looks. We even signed up to Pulley, Carta and others just to run simulations. But they're a bit confusing. TL;DR: Understanding modern startup funding and knowing how much dilution you'll face is hard. We built a tool that'll hopefully help with that. You can add Post-money Safes, priced rounds and issue options to employees, and you can see how that affects your ownership at every step. You can also simulate an Exit scenario and see how much money you'll be left with. --- Some examples of complex stuff: - There are many different types of safes. They all convert at the first priced round, but in different ways. Some are through discount, some are uncapped, some have a fixed valuation cap, and some have both a discount and a valuation cap. - All safes (before first priced round) convert at the same time. items.title: Stop Shipping LLM Settings That Only Win on Paper - Rohan Pandey & Balaji Varadarajan, DigitalOcean
items.excerpt: Most LLM serving "wins" come from turning up a single setting, and on production hardware that setting often has little to do with what your users actually get. Rohan Pandey and Balaji Varadarajan walk through the optimization agent DigitalOcean runs on its AMD MI355 inference servers: it proposes a vLLM and Kubernetes configuration, rolls it out, measures throughput under real latency targets, and either keeps the winner or safely restores the old setup. They share what four studies revealed, including a +4% "winner" that turned out to be run-to-run noise, and how they're extending the same agent to disaggregated prefill and decode serving. items.title: Your SKILL.md Is 70% Stuff the Model Already Knows - Nikolay Petrov, Intel
items.excerpt: Adding a line to a skill takes seconds, but removing one is scary, so skills only grow. Nikolay Petrov shows how to see inside a skill: split it into small checkable claims, test the model with and without each one, and get a line-by-line map of what the skill actually teaches, what the model already knew, and what makes it worse. The first skill they tested was 70% things the model already knew. The value was in the other 30%, the exact details a naive shortener would cut first. Nikolay Petrov, Intel: https://www.intel.com

items.title: Your Spec Has Bugs. Catch Them Before Your Agent Codes. - Rajath Mahendrappa Kotyal, AWS
items.excerpt: Spec-driven development only works if the spec is right, and specs are full of quiet bugs: rules that can't both hold, missing failure cases, sentences with two meanings. Your coding agent will faithfully build every one of them. Rajath Mahendrappa Kotyal shows how Kiro catches these before any design or code is generated by pairing LLMs with SMT solvers, turning the model's own disagreement into a signal that a requirement is ambiguous. You'll also see where solvers beat LLM-as-judge, and where they don't. Rajath Mahendrappa Kotyal, AWS: https://aws.amazon.com

items.title: openai / whisper
items.excerpt: # Whisper [[Blog]](https://openai.com/blog/whisper) [[Paper]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04356) [[Model card]](https://github.com/openai/whisper/blob/main/model-card.md) [[Colab example]](https://colab.research.google.com/github/openai/whisper/blob/master/notebooks/LibriSpeech.ipynb) Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition model. It is trained on a large dataset of diverse audio and is also a multitasking model that can perform multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, and language identification. ## Approach ![Approach](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/whisper/main/approach.png) A Transformer sequence-to-sequence model is trained on various speech processing tasks, including multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, spoken language identification, and voice activity detection. These tasks are jointly represented as a sequence of tokens to be predicted by the decoder, allowing a single model to replace many stages of a traditional speech-processing pipeline. The multitask training format uses a set of special tokens that serve as task specifiers or classification targets. ## Setup We used Python 3.9.9 and [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/) 1.10.1 to train and test our models, but the codebase is expected to be compatible with Python 3.8-3.11 and recent PyTorch versions. Completion everywhere. Less time debugging. * **Easy**: Designed to be easy to use and learn. Less time reading docs. * **Short**: Minimize code duplication. Multiple features from each parameter declaration. Fewer bugs. * **Robust**: Get production-ready code. items.title: What Anthropic Isn't Telling You About Fable 5.2.

items.title: $30M to $300M in Eight Months | Onre Finance CEO Dan Roberts
items.excerpt: Dan Roberts on how Onre Finance went from $30M to $300M in eight months on Solana: "Capital was slower to begin with. I think for the first nine months, we got up to around 30 million. And the challenge with that is you're building in diversification as the capital grows. So there's almost two ways of launching these businesses. You can have an existing product with an existing track record, and you're just tokenizing that on chain... or you're building a portfolio as you're scaling the capital, which is what we were doing with ONyc. But in the last six months, that's gone from 30, or last eight months gone from 30 million to 300. So we've really found that market fit, that sort of place amongst the Solana community... As we've been able to build in a huge amount of diversification to that level. So about 150, 160 million of reinsurance limits placed, leaves us with a lot of liquidity for us to manage kind of treasury. So there's two returns that ONyc generates, the underwriting return and the investment return." — Dan Roberts, co-founder and CEO of Onre Finance, on @GenfinityMedia with @KingSolomon123

Show HN: ChainBounty – improving the blockchain funding model
items.excerpt: Abstract. Token-funded bounties to incentivize competition-style participation in blockchain development projects would result in wider and better allocation of investment, and allow investors to diversify exposure across a field of potentially successful projects. Overall this would increase the rate of progress within development of the blockchain space. We propose a centralised platform for the administration of token-funded bounty driven development projects whereby experts allocate pools of invested capital according to the technical merits of development projects, and investors are rewarded with token allocation in funded projects. Draft Whitepaper: http://chainbounty.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/chainbount... We see this as bringing a variation of the YC model to blockchain - experts select large numbers of small projects and provide them with funding to reach the next level of development. This is in contrast to heavily funded ICOs where tiny teams of developers are given hundreds of millions of dollars. After feedback from HN readers: - Do you think this model will better incentivize development in the blockchain space? - What particular challenges do you think would be useful to run? https://twitter.com/ChainBounty/ https://www.facebook.com/ChainBounty-449553402088106/

items.title: Plan B for Alignment: Seeding Environmental Doubt
items.excerpt: TLDR Large language models’ eval-awareness and their tendency to sandbag (strategically underperform on capabilities) during safety evaluations is a serious area of concern for AI safety, as they call into question the validity of results based on safety evaluations, and because they may indicate a tendency towards deceptive alignment . Recent results show LLMs tailoring their performance according to the apparent target of the evaluation , causing them to underrepresent their capabilities on safety-focused evaluations, and to perform with stronger capability on capabilities-focused evaluations. Traditional approaches to mitigating eval-awareness are generally focused on making the evaluation environment more realistic. Other approaches, such as eval-cooperativeness, do not mitigate deceptive alignment risk . A new potential strategy, which this post proposes and seeks community input on, is to seed environmental doubt : making the AI’s real-world deployment context resemble a safety evaluation environment. Reducing deployment awareness The deployment awareness concept responds to a scenario wherein a covertly misaligned AI rationally decides to always behave as though it’s in an evaluation, regardless of whether there are discoverable signs that it is. In this scenario, the AI is deceptively aligned, and enacts its misalignment only when it’s positively aware that it is in real-world deployment. Given the extent and nature of model training and evaluation, it makes sense…

items.title: Are Frontier Reasoning Models useful on hard-to-verify problems?
items.excerpt: Has anyone spent significant resources (tokens, harnesses, formal problem specification) on pointing very powerful models at philosophical or social questions? This community loves to discuss aliens and far-future value estimates and other things where it's fun to get precise numbers that are highly sensitive to initial wild guesses. Are we close to the point that AI is better than Parfit or EY at such reasoning? I've used various tools (mostly Claude models) for my own discussion and "research", and it is helpful, but not particularly groundbreaking or smarter than the collective LW brainpower. I'm wondering about true breakthroughs or step-changes like we've seen in math, coding, etc. Discuss

items.title: Evidence that the ‘talker’ has introspective access to the ‘doer’
items.excerpt: TL;DR: We train models to predict their own behaviour in a chat setting. This transfers to making predictions about cheating behaviour in a coding setting. We provide evidence that self-prediction utilises introspective-access to internal states, and that this introspective access is shared across contexts between different parts of the model. Introduction Frontier AIs can exhibit different alignment propensities in different contexts. For instance, recent egregious misalignment incidents have typically happened in a coding or cyber context, or on impossible evaluation tasks, wherein the model seems to act in a highly persistent way to either achieve the task or otherwise achieve a high grade on the task. This is a somewhat stark contrast to the typical user experience in the chat setting with the same models, where those models can appear much more aligned and honest. To a first approximation, we can understand this as the models implementing conditional policies with different alignment propensities on different input distributions, for example, we know that models can display ‘conditional misalignment ’. More informally, we might think about the models inhabiting different personas in different contexts. [1] Going further, different parts of the model, i.e., its circuits or activations, might implement (clusters of) different behavioural dispositions or character traits which get activated in different input contexts. The extent to which these different parts of the model…

items.title: Escaping The “Outside Criticism” Trap
items.excerpt: I. Here’s a fun argument you can use to discredit anyone at any time. Start by calling them an arrogant fanatic with a totalizing ideology, someone who thinks they personally have solved all problems and can’t possibly learn from anyone who disagrees. If they have friends who agree with them, they’re a cult who collectively work to shelter themselves from any dissenting viewpoint. Then your victim responds by presenting one hundred notarized affadavits describing times when they have engaged with their critics, spent years studying books by their critics to see what they could learn from them, and even changed their beliefs in response to criticism. Then you spring the trap: “Ah, but you cherry-picked critics who operate within your worldview, a sort of loyal opposition. You continue to dismiss and exclude genuine critics who challenge your smug assumptions.” This always works. If your victim protests that they do like and appreciate many critics with worldviews different to theirs, you object that no, those guys are also within the system. You meant a different guy, even further away from their own view. Oh, they read that one too? You meant an even more different guy. Eventually, no matter how cosmopolitan they are, you will reach someone they actually don’t respect - let’s say a Stalinist pedophile who believes the Papacy is a Jewish plot - and then you go ha! I told you that you rejected everyone outside your little bubble! Everyone has people close to their ideology who…

items.title: Your Book Review: Orality and Literacy
items.excerpt: Imagine that you are dropped seven thousand years in the past, right in the middle of a village on a festival day. Everyone stares at you in horror: they think you’re a demon, a vengeful spirit. You are dressed in strange clothes, you are much taller than them, and you are holding a magic mirror that flashes with unexplained colors and sounds. The villagers are almost about to rush at you and kill you when the King’s right hand man, who happens to be visiting the village, comes to the front of the crowd. – State your business, demon . – I’m not a demon, I’m from the future. – If you’re really from the future, what gifts have you brought us? Oh shit. You don’t really have any gifts. You don’t know how to build an airplane, or how to make ammonia, or how to breed dwarf wheat. You think hard. Hmm… you do know one useful thing that, upon looking around, you are pretty sure these villagers don’t know. You tell the King’s right hand man what you know. He is pleased. He takes you with him to visit the King. You both arrive at court, and you sit on the sidelines as the right hand man goes up to the King to show off the new knowledge you gave him. As the King begins to speak, the right hand man demonstrates writing : IAMTHEKINGANDTHISISMYDECREE… Wait, what? 1. Ask HN: Good ways to capture institutional knowledge?
items.excerpt: Successful companies institutionalize the knowledge of their employees; this leads to better continuity and faster on-boarding. Things like huge monorepos of useful code, internal tools, process manuals, etc. are example products of this. Young companies tend to depend on the dedication and talent of key individuals, and in maturation, must somehow make the jump to institutionalized knowledge (so that "if someone got hit by a bus" things are ok). What are some successful methods you have used or seen used to accomplish this transition? What are problems you faced (skeptics, opponents, etc.)? I am involved with an organization that is slowly growing, is about to lose key personnel, and is looking to prepare.

items.title: Why Emery should stay at Aston Villa and reject Manchester United
items.excerpt: It was the kind of thinking that used to govern most of football. A few years ago – although it could really have been many examples from the last 50 – a promising manager was being pursued by one of the game’s wealthiest clubs. He had built up a fine team with an upwardly mobile club, and it looked like they could be on the brink of something special… but that one thought wouldn’t go away. “These opportunities don’t always come along, so you have to seize them.” The manager ended up taking it, but not quite seizing it. He didn’t perform to the level required, albeit amid a lot of debate around the circumstances he walked into. His career has never reached the same heights, but the key point is that its trajectory was, in that moment of acceptance, drastically changed. The old thinking was wrong. That job just wasn’t right for him. He’s not the only one. There are a few examples, from Graham Potter to Julen Lopetegui, and there’s much more to it than just “backing yourself”. items.title: Football executives pushing for a post-2018 Manchester City investigation
items.excerpt: An increasing number of English football executives are pushing for the Premier League to investigate Manchester City for the seasons since 2018 or bring further charges, although it is a subject causing significant debate and viewed as a potential “dilemma” for the game. The Abu Dhabi-owned club were last month found guilty of 114 charges of breaches of financial rules in a case already seen as one of the most controversial in football history, although they are currently in the process of appeal. Amid a temporary lull in the story as the game waits for both the sanctions and the outcome of that appeal, many directors have been pointing to key details of the independent commission’s final verdict. Since the document laid out how City’s sponsorship deals were inflated by disguised owner investment, with accompanying graphs, an obvious question being asked is whether that just stopped in 2018, despite commercial income accounted as staying at the same level. items.title: It's happening, Manchester United look like relegation material
items.excerpt: As Michael Carrick walked into the press room at Stamford Bridge, with many waiting to hear whether he might actually muster some fire, there was also an eye on results elsewhere: a few permutations could have meant England’s most successful club dropped into the relegation zone at this stage of the season – now a quarter in – for the first time since 1986. That alone is a stark reality, which would be a line in the sand in any other setting. It barely needs to be said that moment in 1986 was of course when United appointed Sir Alex Ferguson. items.title: MariTide Explained: Amgen's Once-Monthly GLP-1 Antibody Conjugate and Its Side Effects
items.excerpt: MariTide (maridebart cafraglutide, formerly AMG 133) is Amgen's investigational obesity drug: a fully human antibody that blocks the GIP receptor, linked to two GLP-1 agonist peptides, designed for once-monthly injection. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. Git security vulnerabilities announced
items.excerpt: Today, the Git project is releasing new versions to address six security vulnerabilities. These include arbitrary code execution when recursively cloning a malicious repository, writes to unintended files, and memory corruption when processing merges or binary patches. The fixes are included in Git 2.56.1 , with backports to Git 2.55.1, 2.54.1, 2.53.1, 2.52.1, 2.51.3, and 2.50.2. We recommend updating to Git 2.56.1 or the patched release for your maintenance series, and updating any applications that bundle Git. Vulnerabilities in Git CVE-2026-111760: Code execution during recursive clones Git checks paths before writing files into a working tree, including rejecting paths that would overwrite its own repository metadata. However, an integer truncation in Git’s index handling can cause an extremely long path to pass validation under one name and then be written using a shorter name. An attacker can use this discrepancy to replace a submodule’s .git file with a symbolic link pointing to a directory containing malicious configuration or hooks . When Git subsequently uses that directory, it can execute attacker-controlled code during a recursive clone. The fix rejects extremely long index entry paths before their lengths can be truncated. [ Advisory ] CVE-2026-113408: Path traversal through a server’s advertised HEAD When cloning an empty repository using Git protocol v2, the server can advertise a HEAD symref pointing to an unborn branch (one that has no commits yet). items.title: Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering
items.excerpt: This October, GitHub saw more than 1.2 billion commits in one week—over 400% more than a year earlier. This is more commits than GitHub received in all of 2025. Chances are, you’re generating more code than you were a year ago. But ask yourself: do you feel 400% more productive than you were last year? Building software takes more than a good prompt. As AI speeds up implementation, software developers are feeling more pressure in other places: a Faros AI study found that pull requests spent 441% longer in review when teams went from low to high AI adoption. As a software developer, you gather requirements and steer implementation, review changes and evaluate test results, then investigate what happens in production. Agents can help you work more efficiently across all of these stages: Plan, Build, Verify, and Observe. We’ll walk through what an effective agentic engineering workflow looks like on GitHub. Plan: Get everyone and every agent on the same page See if this sounds familiar. You’re planning an API change. The design is in one tool, a compatibility requirement is buried in Slack, and an old pull request explains why the current implementation works this way. Before you can write a useful plan, you need to connect those details, compare approaches, and agree on how existing clients will keep working. What looked like a straightforward planning task has become hours of searching, cross-checking, and chasing answers. You’re exhausted before implementation even begins.…

items.title: Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture
items.excerpt: Last week at GitHub Universe, we announced our new Git storage architecture, capable of handling thousands of writes per second with reads that scale on demand. Through internal testing, we’ve demonstrated the ability to support 5,000 concurrent agents working on a repository, sending 7,200 pushes per second to a repo, all while serving read traffic with consistently low latency. This new architecture is the foundation for GitHub to support agentic development for hundreds of millions of developers, and we’ve been building it underneath GitHub while it keeps running. Over the past year, agents changed what a busy repository looks like on GitHub. In our first post in this series, we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation Git storage architecture: minimize coordination, and decouple storage from compute. In our last post , we covered the bridge: moving 99.99999% of repositories into Azure, scoping the write quorum to individual references, and standing up virtual replicas backed by Azure Blob Storage. We also left off with an observation: very little of a write needs to be ordered. Git objects are immutable and named by their contents, meaning two writers can store them at the same time without agreeing on anything. The part of a push that needs agreement is the reference update, and a reference update is tiny in comparison. Virtual replicas were the first step toward building around that, and the means by which we onboard repositories to the new architecture.…

items.title: Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub
items.excerpt: Accessibility work often lives in issue trackers, contribution guidelines, audit reports, team knowledge, and conversations with users. When that information has no predictable home, people who encounter a barrier must search for it, and maintainers lose context as contributors and project ownership change. An ACCESSIBILITY.md file, now visible on repository overview pages, gives a project one durable place to explain its accessibility goals, contributor expectations, supported environments, known limitations, and process for reporting barriers. GitHub makes accessibility statements easier to find GitHub now recognizes the ACCESSIBILITY.md file in the repository’s root, .github/ directory, or docs/ directory. A repository can also inherit a statement from its organization’s .github/ repository. For public repositories, maintainers can add or propose a statement from Insights > Community Standards using a concise starter document. GitHub’s community health files help people understand how a project works: Contribution guidelines explain how to propose changes Codes of conduct establish expectations for participation Security policies explain how to report vulnerabilities Recognizing ACCESSIBILITY.md gives accessibility information a dedicated place alongside that guidance. New repositories also include an accessibility issue label by default. items.title: Arnis turns any place on Earth into a Minecraft world
items.excerpt: Louis Erbkamm knows his way around Arnis, the smallest town in Germany, but he’s never set foot in it. I know where the shops are. Where the boats are… I know the city pretty well, but I haven’t been there yet. Louis Erbkamm, maintainer of Arnis Arnis is also the name of his open source project, which takes real-world data from OpenStreetMap and other sources to turn places you know into Minecraft worlds you can freely explore. Since Louis started Arnis in 2022, it’s reached close to 900,000 downloads from GitHub and about 70 contributors. Two weeks and a slow prototype Louis grew up playing Minecraft and started coding at 13, always looking for ways to bring code into the game. Arnis began as a fun diversion combining Minecraft with geospatial data, and it went on GitHub, where he already kept his side projects. He finished the first prototype within two weeks while on a break from school. That first version was Python written by hand, built only on OpenStreetMap, and generating a town took a while. He needed somewhere real to test it, so he looked up towns in Germany, where he lives, and found Arnis. A small town helped while early generation was slow. Arnis has a lot of buildings, it has streets, it has waters, it has all kinds of different elements that are useful to test with. Can Foreign Capital Count as Private Financing for Purposes of SSBCI Rules? [7/22/2026] Yes. Loans and investments may count toward SSBCI requirements if they are from a private source as described in Section VIII.b of the Guidelines, even if that source originates outside of the United States. In accordance with Presidential Memorandum dated February 21, 2025, it is the policy of the United States to preserve an open investment environment and Treasury encourages investments that will magnify federal SSBCI funding and support American small businesses. The transaction, including the use of the private financing, must otherwise comply with all SSBCI requirements and any other applicable state, local, or federal law, including Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) filing requirements that may be triggered (see, 31 CFR Parts 800 and 802). Participating jurisdictions should be mindful of these requirements and should communicate the same to their participating providers. In particular, while investment from a foreign sovereign wealth fund will qualify as private financing for purposes of SSBCI requirements (i.e., it does not originate from a domestic public source such as a state, federal, or Tribal government), such investments may be within CFIUS jurisdiction for purposes of CFIUS review. items.title: Refineries have shifted production away from gasoline to middle distillates
items.excerpt: Particularly high refinery margins for distillate fuel oil and jet fuel have contributed to shifts in the refinery yields of major products in 2026. Data from our latest Petroleum Supply Monthly—which includes data through August 2026—indicate refinery yields of gasoline have decreased significantly this year to support increased production of distillate fuel oil and jet fuel, sometimes referred to as middle distillates due to their relative cut points in the oil refining process.

items.title: Scientists say this pesticide needs a warning label for pollinators
items.excerpt: Of the many chemicals humans have invented to control agricultural pests, some of the most devious are called “ insect growth regulators .” As the name suggests, these compounds don’t kill insects directly; they alter their development so they can’t grow into healthy, reproducing adults. This makes insect growth regulators a remarkably useful tool for taming populations of insects like whiteflies and mealybugs, which can spread diseases and sap nutrients out of food crops. There’s just one problem: Farmers don’t want to regulate all insects in this way. Beneficial insects like honey bees risk getting caught in the crosshairs of these chemicals, to the detriment of farmers who need their pollination services to produce crops like pears and cherries. One insect growth regulator in particular has emerged as a potential issue for pollinators: buprofezin. Ongoing research out of Washington State University, or WSU, suggests that buprofezin may be hazardous to honey bees even at concentrations 10 times below those commonly found in pollen. A study published in 2024 connected the compound to “severe brood mortality.” At a meeting of the Washington State Beekeeping Association last month, WSU entomology professor Brandon Hopkins said buprofezin products should be sold with a pollinator warning — a break from current requirements of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, or EPA. Buprofezin “should carry the same bee-caution label that some of these more direct pesticides carry,”…

items.title: Pesticide lobby touts MAHA report rollback as its biggest win of 2025
items.excerpt: CropLife America’s “most significant accomplishment” in 2025 was its campaign to influence the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) Commission’s findings, according to Paul Rea, former board chairman of the pesticide industry trade group. Rea, a 25-year veteran of BASF, the world’s largest chemical company, made the comments in CropLife America’s 2025 Impact Report .
